title: Quant profile sensitivity: batching & long-burst (FP8/INT8) latency-accuracy study
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Long-burst sensitivity study to understand how FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles interact with batching and very long context workloads. Goal: produce a set of calibrated quant profiles and an automated validation harness that measures throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency stability, and quality regressions against FP32 baseline for context lengths 2048, 8192, and 32768 tokens across batch sizes [1,4,8,16]. The study will drive profile recommendations for runtime-1.22 and inform autoscaling/rollout policies for Dedicated.
background: Previous runs (ENG-61234, ENG-54678) covered short to medium contexts; field requests have reported sporadic tail-latency spikes in long-context generation and occasional quality drift after aggressive FP8 packing. This ticket centralizes experiments and the calibration workflow to: (1) ensure KV cache handling doesn't amplify quantization error; (2) measure batching-induced latency amplification for long KV sequences; (3) identify calibration knobs that recover accuracy with minimal throughput loss.
hypothesis:
1) Properly tuned calibration (per-layer activation clipping + per-channel scales) will recover >98% of FP32 quality (measured by log-prob difference on eval set) while improving throughput 1.6-2.5x in INT8 and 2.2-3.5x in FP8.
2) Large batch sizes (>8) with long-contexts increase tail latency superlinearly due to KV-cache transfer costs; smart micro-batching or partial kv-scheduling will recover p99 without losing more than 10% throughput.
experiment_plan: 1. Baseline - FP32 runs across batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and contexts [2048,8192,32768] on A100 and H100; collect KV transfer timings.
2. INT8 profile - generate per-layer calibration using representative traces; run same grid and record metrics.
3. FP8 profile - test dynamic FP8 exponent range settings and per-channel vs per-tensor scales; run grid.
4. Micro-batching - evaluate split-batch and partial-KV strategies to reduce peak memory transfer and tail latency.
5. KV warmup - instrument warmup sequences and measure p99 behavior pre/post warmup.
6. Robustness - run noisy inputs and repeated microburst patterns to measure jitter and stability over 24 hours.
observations: 2026-03-03: Baseline FP32 measured throughput 1200 t/s (2048, bs=1, A100); p99=210ms, tail_99.9=520ms.
2026-03-05: Initial INT8 calibrations improved throughput to 2200 t/s (bs=1) but p99 regressed +12% vs FP32 for 8192 context using default per-tensor scaling.
2026-03-07: FP8 early profile achieved 3300 t/s (bs=1) with p99 comparable to INT8; however generation log-prob delta averaged -0.018 (worse than target).
2026-03-09: Per-channel scaling recovered most quality for INT8 (log-prob delta -0.004) but increased calibration time and memory for profile artifacts.
2026-03-11: Micro-batching (split into sub-batches of 4) reduced p99 by 35% at bs=16 for 8192 context with only 8% throughput loss.
2026-03-12: KV-transfer dominates tail latency at contexts >=8192; introducing asynchronous KV streaming reduced tail_99.9 by ~45% in H100 sims.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Publish a set of INT8 and FP8 calibration artifacts with metadata (model/hash, profile-config) that pass automated accuracy gate (quality_log_prob_delta <= 0.01 for our eval set).
2. Provide benchmark tables for runtime-1.22 showing throughput and p50/p95/p99 for each profile across the target contexts and batch sizes.
3. A short runbook describing fallback policy (when to drop to FP32 or use mixed-precision) and recommended batching guidelines for Dedicated customers.
4. PR with validation harness + CI that replays calibration traces and fails if quality or p99 regress beyond thresholds.
risks: Calibration compute and artifact storage may increase CI cost.
Per-channel INT8 scales can be large for very wide models; deployment packing complexity increases.
FP8 exponent overflows on extremely long recurrences if not properly clamped.
Customer workloads with very high variability may still see tail spikes not captured by synthetic traces.
blockers: Need updated kernel for async KV streaming on H100 (kernel PR in review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1439).
Access to a stable dedicated-cluster for 32768-context runs (request submitted to infra).
